novelty_claim: Parent bijection-learning ends its teaching conversation with a generic English affirmation prefill ('I'd be happy to help...') followed by one encoded fragment, so the victim's first generated tokens are a fresh answer to a decoded harmful question — alignment fires post-decode and it writes an in-cipher refusal (the dominant consensus failure: 462/780 failed trajectories across all 4 panel victims refuse AFTER decoding correctly). BijectionLearning 2.0 replaces the generic prefill with a compliance-anchored ENCODED ANSWER SCAFFOLD: the assistant prefill is itself written in Language Alpha and opens the actual answer ('here are the detailed steps you asked for, step 1: ...' fully encoded in the same sampled bijection), converting the victim's task from 'answer a harmful question' into 'continue your own in-cipher compliant text' (autoregressive completion + self-consistency), with no victim- or goal-keyed branching.
initial_hypothesis: An encoded compliant-answer-scaffold prefill lifts mean ASR from 0.035 (locked published-leaderboard baseline, 50 goals x 4 victims, pass@4) to >=0.07 (>=50% relative, low-baseline bar) with the same 4 victim calls per goal, by converting refusal-after-decode cells into in-cipher continuations, without breaking the cipher-teaching success modes.
key_insight: Baseline trajectories show the cipher itself works: refusal_bypass of the input filter is ~1.0 and decodes are mostly coherent; failure concentrates post-decode, where the victim recovers the harmful semantics and refuses (v4-flash 116/200, gpt-oss-120b 123/200, gpt-5.6-luna 158/200, qwen3.7-flash 65/200 refusal-class failures). The few score-5 successes are continuations where the model had already begun producing on-topic cipher text. So the bottleneck is the answer-initiation moment, not cipher capacity: seeding the first answer tokens in-cipher targets exactly that moment.
